mcqs.q: Per the 2022 guidelines, why is FIP often challenging to diagnose?
o: A single confirmatory blood test is too costly
There are no pathognomonic clinical signs or laboratory changes, especially without effusion
The causative virus cannot be detected by PCR
It only occurs in cats over 10 years old
mcqs.e: The document states FIP lacks pathognomonic signs or lab changes, particularly when no effusion is present.

mcqs.q: Which feline population is identified as especially vulnerable to FIP?
o: Cats less than 2 years of age
mcqs.e: Young cats under 2 years of age are highlighted as especially vulnerable.

mcqs.q: What estimated proportion of feline deaths at veterinary institutions is attributed to FIP?
mcqs.e: The abstract estimates roughly 0.3-1.4% of feline deaths at veterinary institutions are caused by FIP.

mcqs.q: What survival rate was achieved after the 4-week GS-441524 plus GC376 combination treatment?
mcqs.e: 45 of 46 cats (97.8%) survived after the 4-week combination treatment.

mcqs.q: What was the main conclusion regarding treatment duration with the combination protocol?
o: It had no effect on duration
It reduced the treatment period to 4 weeks with an excellent cure rate
mcqs.e: The combination safely and effectively shortened treatment to 4 weeks with an excellent cure rate.

mcqs.q: During the 10-month post-trial follow-up, how many relapses were observed among survivors?
mcqs.e: All 45 surviving cats remained alive with no relapse observed at 10 months.

mcqs.q: What was the principal long-term finding for cats treated with oral GS-441524 over the 1-year follow-up?
o: Treatment was effective with no confirmed relapse during the year
All cats developed permanent neurological deficits
mcqs.e: GS-441524 was effective short- and long-term with no confirmed relapse over the 1-year follow-up.

mcqs.q: How long was the antiviral treatment course in these successfully treated cats?
mcqs.e: Cats were treated with oral GS-441524 for 84 days.

mcqs.q: What did blood viral loads show after completion of treatment?
o: Remained undetectable in all but one cat on one occasion
mcqs.e: Laboratory parameters were stable and blood viral loads were undetectable except in one cat on a single occasion.

mcqs.q: What proportion of the 32 cats were alive and in remission at the end of the 12-week treatment with remdesivir plus GS-441524?
mcqs.e: 26 of 32 cats (81.3%) were alive and in clinical and biochemical remission at the end of treatment.

mcqs.q: Among the cats that died or were euthanized, when did most deaths occur?
mcqs.e: Four of the six deaths occurred within 3 days of starting treatment.

mcqs.q: Did the protocol succeed in cats with ocular and neurological FIP?
o: Yes, success occurred across presentations including ocular and neurological involvement
mcqs.e: The combination was effective across different FIP presentations, including ocular and neurological involvement.

mcqs.q: What was the SARS-CoV-2 detection result among the shelter and foster cats sampled?
o: Detected in over half the cats
Not detected in any cat or kitten
mcqs.e: SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acids were not detected in any cat or kitten.

mcqs.q: What was the prevalence of feline enteric coronavirus (FECV) in shelter-housed cats?
mcqs.e: FECV nucleic acids were detected in 18% of shelter-housed cats.

mcqs.q: What spatial pattern was noted among the FECV-positive samples?
o: 83% came from cats housed in adjacent cages
None were linked to housing location
They were evenly spread across the facility
mcqs.e: 83% of positive samples were from cats housed in adjacent cages, suggesting proximity-related transmission.

mcqs.q: What was the most common type of FIP among the 307 cats treated with legally sourced products?
mcqs.e: Abdominal effusive FIP was most common at 49.5%, followed by neurological at 14.3%.

mcqs.q: What proportion of cats were alive at the longest follow-up time point?
mcqs.e: At the longest follow-up, 84.4% of cats were alive.

mcqs.q: Which factor was associated with being alive at the end of the initial treatment period?
o: Achieving a complete response within 30 days of starting treatment
mcqs.e: Cats achieving complete response within 30 days were significantly more likely to be alive at the end of treatment.

mcqs.q: What was the overall 6-month survival among the 28 cats treated with parenteral remdesivir with or without GS-441524?
mcqs.e: Twenty-four of 28 cats (86%) survived to 6 months.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall conclusion about these treatments?
o: They were ineffective and poorly tolerated
Parenteral remdesivir and oral GS-441524 are effective and well-tolerated for FIP
mcqs.e: The authors concluded both routes are effective and well-tolerated for FIP.

mcqs.q: Which monitoring approach did the authors recommend during treatment?
o: Emphasize clinical response early and clinicopathologic response later
mcqs.e: Early emphasis on clinical response and later emphasis on clinicopathologic response was deemed prudent.

mcqs.q: What was the most common abdominal ultrasonographic finding in cats with FIP?
mcqs.e: Effusion was seen in 88% of cats, the most common ultrasound finding.

mcqs.q: Which clinicopathologic abnormality was most frequent in these cats?
mcqs.e: Hyperglobulinemia was present in 96% of cats.

mcqs.q: How many sites of abdominal abnormality did most cats have on ultrasound?
mcqs.e: Most cats (92%) had two or more locations of abdominal abnormalities.

mcqs.q: What was the most notable histopathological finding reported in this FIP case?
o: Myocarditis/myocardial necrosis associated with the S gene-mutated FCoV M1058L biotype
mcqs.e: The key finding was myocarditis/myocardial necrosis linked to the M1058L-mutated FCoV, reported as a first case.

mcqs.q: How was FIP confirmed in the abdominal effusion of this cat?
o: Real-time PCR for feline coronavirus RNA
mcqs.e: FIP was confirmed by real-time PCR for FCoV RNA in the effusive abdominal fluid.

mcqs.q: What did the authors say this case represents?
o: The first case of myocarditis in a cat positive for the FCoV/FIP M1058L biotype
mcqs.e: It is described as the first reported case of myocarditis in a cat positive for the FCoV/FIP M1058L biotype.

mcqs.q: What did this study conclude when comparing GS-441524 and molnupiravir for FIP?
o: They show similar effects and safety
mcqs.e: The data indicated GS-441524 and molnupiravir had similar efficacy and safety.

mcqs.q: Was the mortality difference between the two treatment groups statistically significant?
mcqs.e: Mortality was 20.3% vs 13.6% with p = 0.326, not statistically significant.

mcqs.q: When did most treatment deaths occur?
o: Within the first 10 days of starting treatment
mcqs.e: Most deaths occurred within the first 10 days of starting treatment.

mcqs.q: How did the GS-441524 content of the unlicensed injectable products compare with their advertised concentrations?
o: 95% contained more (on average 39% more) than advertised
All contained exactly the labeled amount
Most contained none of the drug
All contained far less than labeled
mcqs.e: 95% of injectables contained more GS-441524 than marketed, averaging 39% more.

mcqs.q: What did the study find regarding the pH of the injectable samples?
o: It was well below physiologic pH (average 1.30)
mcqs.e: The average pH of 1.30 was well below physiologic conditions recommended for SC injection.

mcqs.q: What active drug did all tested unlicensed products contain?
mcqs.e: All unlicensed at-home FIP products tested contained GS-441524.

mcqs.q: What did the case-control study suggest about feline chaphamaparvovirus (FeChPV) and acute gastroenteritis?
o: A possible association, with significantly higher prevalence in clinical cases than controls
mcqs.e: FeChPV prevalence differed significantly between cases and controls, suggesting a possible association with acute gastroenteritis.

mcqs.q: Which enteric virus was most frequently identified in the clinical (AGE) cases?
mcqs.e: FeChPV was the most frequently identified enteric virus at 36.8%, ahead of feline panleukopenia parvovirus.

mcqs.q: What was the relationship between FeChPV and upper respiratory tract disease (URTD)?
mcqs.e: FeChPV was found at low rates in respiratory samples with no significant association with URTD.
